finding.title: Replace the wildcard `case _:` on the sealed AsyncValue switch in gamification_screen_l1_test.dart
finding.why: AsyncValue is `sealed class AsyncValue<T>` with exactly 3 subtypes (AsyncData/AsyncLoading/AsyncError, verified in the riverpod package source). This switch handles AsyncData and AsyncError explicitly but falls back to a `case _:` wildcard for AsyncLoading instead of naming it. Per docs/coding-standards.md:197-199 (EH-6), a wildcard arm 'silently absorbs future variants and destroys' the compiler's exhaustiveness guarantee — here it also hides that the loading case is deliberately made to hang (Completer().future never completes) rather than being an oversight.
finding.recommendation: Change `case _:` to `case AsyncLoading():` so the switch is explicitly exhaustive.
acceptance_criteria: The switch in _buildApp's achievementsOverviewProvider override names AsyncLoading() explicitly instead of using a wildcard arm.

finding.title: Delete or consolidate the 11 duplicate coverage groups in test/features/labels/domain_term_rendering_modes_test.dart
finding.rule: AG-5 (test/ mirrors lib/ 1:1) + Fowler duplication + TQ-1 pyramid

evidence.quote: group('Layer 4f — track-order container section header word', () {

finding.why: This file lives in test/features/labels/, which has no lib/features/labels/ counterpart (labels are a core/labels/ concern) — one of the AG-5-flagged unmirrored test directories. Every one of its 11 groups re-pins a Hebrew-terms/nusach behavior that is already asserted, often with byte-identical fixture literals or the same override-class names, at the widget/module's correctly mirrored path: L1(primaryUnitLabel/containerCountLabel)->test/core/constants/curriculum_label_variant_test.dart:145-192; L2(chazara/shabbos)->test/core/labels/domain_term_labels_vocab_test.dart; L3a(CurriculumListScreen counts '1 Masekhtot'/'1 Mishnayot')->curriculum_list_screen_test.dart:98-155 (identical strings + comment wording); L3b(ScopeSelectionScreen chumash 'Sefer')->scope_lifetime_l1_test.dart:184-269 (identical override classes _HebrewTermsOn/_HebrewTermsOff/_VariantAshkenazi/_VariantSephardi and the same Chumash fixture); L4a(HierarchyProgressCard Tahorot/Taharos)->progress_widgets_test.dart:430-453 (identical fixture + identical comment 'Tahoros/Tahorot is the ONE seder that differs across nuschaot'); L4b(SiyumimGroupedView 'Siyum Seder Taharos'/'Tahorot')->siyumim_grouped_view_test.dart:341-421 (identical aggregateKey 'Tahorot' fixture and identical expect() strings); L4c(GoalSetupForm Dafim/Dapim)->goal_setup_screen_test.dart:262-318; L4d(SacredTimeLockOverlay 'Good Shabbos'/'Good Shabbat'/שבת)->sacred_time_lock_overlay_l10n_test.dart:69-114; L4e(SacredTimeSettingsCard header)->sacred_time_settings_card_l10n_test.dart:198-271; L4f(containerSectionHeader)->curriculum_labels_extended_test.dart:106-123 and curriculum_defaults_extended_test.dart:131-158; L4g(CurriculumLabel.curriculum Mishnayos/Mishnayot)->curriculum_label_test.dart:39-66. Concrete cost: every future change to a label/nusach format now has two call sites to update; a contributor who edits only the mirrored file (the one AG-5 says to look for) leaves this file's copy silently untouched until a full-suite run — the exact 'cross-wave drift' AG-2/AG-5's own rationale is written to prevent — and a contributor searching test/features/<feature>/ for a widget's coverage (the AG-5 contract) will not find this file at all since 'labels' isn't a real feature.
finding.recommendation: For each of the 11 groups, confirm the mirrored file's assertion is equivalent (9 of 11 already confirmed identical above) and delete the group here; if the file is kept as a deliberate single 'classB regression index' (its own header states these were 'found by hand + on-device'), say so explicitly and have each surviving group's comment cross-reference the mirrored file it also lives in, so the next audit wave does not add a 12th copy of the same pin.
acceptance_criteria: flutter test on test/features/labels/, test/core/labels/, test/core/constants/, and the seven touched test/features/<feature>/ dirs still passes, and the total expect( count across old+new locations for the removed groups does not decrease (TQ-7 ratchet — no assertion is lost, only the duplicate copy).

AG-5's pending checker ('[Pending] audit check for unmirrored test files' per coding-standards.md AG-5) is implemented and either passes clean for this path or the file carries an explicit exemption comment analogous to the story_acceptance/ carve-out already written into the AG-5 rule text.
No two files under test/ contain an identical expect(find.text(...)) string-literal pin for the same widget + mode combination among the 11 pairs cited in evidence.

finding.title: Cut test/features/labels/domain_term_rendering_modes_test.dart from 1088 hand-written lines to the AG-3 400-line cap

evidence.quote: // Runtime-confidence layer for the Hebrew-terms enforcement.

finding.why: The file is 1088 hand-written, non-generated lines — 2.72x the 400-line AG-3 ratchet — built from five separate local _build*App/_pumpProbe factories (lines 168-417) plus per-mode literal maps repeated across 11 groups instead of a shared pump helper. At this size the tail (Layers 4d-4g, lines ~883-1072) sits outside a typical single-file agent read budget, which is exactly the failure mode AG-3's stated rationale (content past the window is invisible, becomes a dumping ground) describes, and is corroborated by the finding above: the file grew by repeated append-only accretion across audit waves rather than being kept to one purpose.
finding.recommendation: Applying the companion duplication finding (delete the ~11 redundant groups) removes most of the file's bulk as a side effect. If any layer is kept as the sole owner of its assertion, move it into its own file under the correctly mirrored path (e.g. a Layer-1/2 pure-function file under test/core/labels/ or test/core/constants/) rather than re-growing this file.
acceptance_criteria: find learning_tracker/test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' (the AG-3 checker text from coding-standards.md AG-3) no longer lists this file.

finding.title: Split completion_writer.dart and completion_repository_impl.dart under the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: completion_writer.dart is 770 lines and completion_repository_impl.dart (a churn HOTSPOT) is 891 lines, both hand-written and both nearly double the 400-line cap. Large single-responsibility-violating files raise the odds any single edit misses a related branch (exactly the class of bug the batch's other findings are drawn from) and slow every future review.
finding.recommendation: Extract CompletionWriter's batch-resurrection/upgrade helpers (_resurrectTombstone, _upgradePriorMarkRow, the natural-key helpers) into a co-located mixin/helper class; extract CompletionRepositoryImpl's bookmark-advance and siyum-dispatch orchestration (_advanceBookmark, _dispatchSiyumDetectionForRefs, _bulkSourceFor) into a separate collaborator so the repository itself shrinks toward the 400-line target.
acceptance_criteria: AG-3 line-count checker (pending) reports both files ≤400 lines, or each carries a `// linelimit-ok: <reason>` waiver with a stated reason.

finding.title: Inject BookmarkRepository (with its ContentIndex) into CompletionRepositoryImpl instead of ad-hoc-constructing it for delegated profiles
finding.why: _advanceBookmark only uses the DI-injected BookmarkRepository (wired with a ContentIndex for O(1) adjacent-item lookups via bookmarkRepositoryProvider) when the target profile equals the active session profile. For any delegated-profile completion — BulkCompletionRequest.profileId is documented for exactly this: 'add track for a child while the session active profile differs' and bulk_prior_completion_service.dart exercises it from onboarding — the code instead `new`s a fresh BookmarkRepositoryImpl without passing contentIndex:, silently falling onto the documented O(N) full-curriculum scan fallback on every bookmark advance. completion_repository_impl.dart also directly imports another feature repository (bookmark_repository_impl.dart), the pattern SM-8 exists to prevent. completion_repository_impl_test.dart's setUp never injects a bookmarkRepository at all, so this branch (and the fast/slow-path difference) is exercised by every test in the file yet never asserted — a regression here would ship silently.
finding.recommendation: Thread a `BookmarkRepository Function(int profileId)` factory (or the ContentIndex itself) into CompletionRepositoryImpl via its constructor/provider, matching how completionRepositoryProvider already injects CompletionDetectionService, instead of constructing BookmarkRepositoryImpl by hand inside _advanceBookmark.
acceptance_criteria: completion_repository_impl_test.dart gains a case with bookmarkProfileId != activeProfileId that asserts the ContentIndex fast path is used (e.g. mockContentRepository.getContentForCurriculum is not called when a ContentIndex is supplied).
